overview: Black plays ...a6 at once to stop Nb5 and prepare ...b5, keeping the choice between ...e6 (Kan) and ...Nf6/...d6 (Najdorf) for later. After 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 the game usually transposes to a Kan or Najdorf; White's alternatives 3.c3 (Venice) and 3.Nc3 (Yerevan) steer into Alapin- or Closed-style positions. Black's plan is queenside space and the c-file; White's is to use the d4 knight and kingside space.

white_ideas.idea: 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 and play Najdorf-type attacks with Be3/f3/Qd2 or Bg5.
3.c3 e6 4.d4 d5 and an Alapin-style centre, avoiding Open Sicilian theory.

black_ideas.idea: ...b5 and ...Bb7 queenside expansion, with ...a6 denying Nb5/Bb5.
Delay ...e6 or ...d6 to keep Kan, Najdorf or Taimanov set-ups available.

typical_structures.structure: Open Sicilian after 3.d4: White d4 knight, Black d6/e6 chain with half-open c-file.

character.notes: Mostly transposes to Kan/Najdorf-type positions, which are double-edged but not as forcing as Najdorf main lines.

soundness.notes: Fully sound; a flexible move order.

structure.notes: Open Sicilian asymmetry with a half-open c-file, so semi-open.

approach.notes: A move-order choice inside the Sicilian, played by strong players.

level.notes: Need to know the Kan/Najdorf structures, but the extra move order adds little memory load.
